items.name: Commutative laws (propositional)
items.latex: p\wedge q\equiv q\wedge p,\qquad p\vee q\equiv q\vee p

items.name: Associative laws (propositional)
items.latex: (p\wedge q)\wedge r\equiv p\wedge(q\wedge r),\qquad(p\vee q)\vee r\equiv p\vee(q\vee r)

items.name: Distributive laws (propositional)
items.latex: p\wedge(q\vee r)\equiv(p\wedge q)\vee(p\wedge r),\qquad p\vee(q\wedge r)\equiv(p\vee q)\wedge(p\vee r)

items.name: De Morgan's laws (propositional)
items.body:
$\sim(p\wedge q)\equiv\sim p\vee\sim q,\qquad\sim(p\vee q)\equiv\sim p\wedge\sim q$
`!(p && q) == (!p || !q), !(p || q) == (!p && !q)`

items.name: Law of implication
items.note: Key step in removing => while simplifying a wff

items.name: Law of excluded middle
items.note: Always true: a tautology

items.name: Law of contradiction
items.note: Always false: a contradiction

items.name: Simplification with tautology and contradiction
items.latex: p\wedge T\equiv p,\quad p\vee T\equiv T,\quad p\wedge F\equiv F,\quad p\vee F\equiv p
items.note: T = any tautology, F = any contradiction

items.name: Idempotent laws (propositional)
items.latex: p\wedge p\equiv p,\qquad p\vee p\equiv p

items.name: Absorption laws (propositional)
items.latex: p\vee(p\wedge q)\equiv p,\qquad p\wedge(p\vee q)\equiv p

items.name: Converse of an implication
items.note: Not equivalent to the original implication

items.name: Inverse of an implication
items.note: Not equivalent to the original; equivalent to the converse

items.name: Contrapositive
items.latex: \text{Contrapositive of }p\Rightarrow q\text{ is }\sim q\Rightarrow\sim p\ \equiv\ p\Rightarrow q
items.note: Always logically equivalent to the original

items.name: Implication with F antecedent or T consequent
items.latex: F\Rightarrow q\equiv T,\qquad p\Rightarrow T\equiv T
items.note: Vacuous truth

items.name: Chain rule (hypothetical syllogism)
items.note: A tautology

items.name: Modus ponens
items.note: A tautology: from p and p=>q infer q

items.name: Modus tollens
items.note: A tautology: from p=>q and not q infer not p

items.name: Distributive law (OR over AND)
items.note: Unlike ordinary algebra, + distributes over . too

items.name: Duality principle
items.note: If an identity is true, its dual is also true; variables are not complemented

items.name: Consensus theorem (POS form)
items.note: Dual of the consensus theorem

items.name: Complement of a Boolean expression
items.note: e.g. complement of AB + C is (A' + B')C'

items.name: Precedence of Boolean operators
items.note: Brackets first; A + B.C means A + (B.C)

items.name: Verifying a law by truth table
items.latex: \text{LHS}=\text{RHS}\iff\text{output columns identical for all }2^{n}\text{ input rows}

items.name: Number of Boolean functions
items.latex: n\text{ variables}\Rightarrow2^{n}\text{ input combinations and }2^{2^{n}}\text{ distinct functions}
items.note: 2 variables: 16 functions; 3 variables: 256

items.latex: m_i=\text{AND of all }n\text{ variables: bit }1\to X,\ \text{bit }0\to\overline{X}
items.note: m5 (101) = A B' C; index = binary value with first variable as MSB

items.name: Maxterm
items.latex: M_i=\text{OR of all }n\text{ variables: bit }0\to X,\ \text{bit }1\to\overline{X}

items.name: Canonical SOP
items.note: Sum of minterms; each term contains every variable

items.name: Canonical POS
items.note: Product of maxterms; each term contains every variable

items.name: Cardinal (shorthand) representation
items.note: List only the decimal indices of the minterms or maxterms

items.name: SOP and POS conversion

items.name: Expanding to canonical form
items.latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{Missing variable }X:\ \text{multiply a product term by }(X+\overline{X});\ \text{add }X\overline{X}\text{ }\\&\text{to a sum term}\end{aligned}
items.note: e.g. A = A(B + B') = AB + AB'

items.name: Standard SOP and POS forms
items.latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{SOP: OR of AND terms, e.g. }AB+\overline{A}C;\qquad\text{POS: AND of OR terms, e.g. }(A+B)(\overline{A}\\&+C)\end{aligned}
items.note: Terms need not contain all variables (unlike canonical forms)

items.name: Number of K-map cells
items.note: Each cell is one minterm (SOP) or maxterm (POS)

items.name: Gray code order on K-map
items.note: Adjacent labels differ in exactly one bit

items.latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{Adjacent cells differ in exactly one variable;\ edges wrap }\\&\text{around (left-right, top-bottom, four corners)}\end{aligned}

items.name: Group size in a K-map
items.note: Groups must be rectangular and a power of 2

items.name: Variables eliminated by a group
items.latex: \text{Group of }2^{k}\text{ cells eliminates }k\text{ variables; term has }n-k\text{ literals}
items.note: Pair: 1 variable; quad: 2; octet: 3

items.name: Cells covered by a product term
items.latex: \text{Product term with }k\text{ literals in }n\text{ variables covers }2^{n-k}\text{ cells}

items.name: K-map grouping rules
items.latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{Group the 1s (SOP) in the largest possible power-of-2 }\\&\text{rectangles; groups may overlap; cover every 1; no diagonal }\\&\text{groups}\end{aligned}

items.name: Reading an SOP from a K-map
items.latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{Each group}\to\text{AND of variables that stay constant (}1\to X,\ 0\to\overline{X});\ F=\text{OR }\\&\text{of group terms}\end{aligned}

items.name: Reading a POS from a K-map
items.latex: \text{Group the 0s; each group}\to\text{OR term (}0\to X,\ 1\to\overline{X});\ F=\text{AND of the terms}

items.name: Four corners of a 4-variable K-map
items.latex: m_0,\ m_2,\ m_8,\ m_{10}\ \text{form one quad}=\overline{B}\,\overline{D}

items.name: Prime and essential prime implicants
items.latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{Prime implicant: a group not contained in a larger group;\ }\\&\text{essential: covers a 1 no other prime implicant covers}\end{aligned}

items.name: Recursion rule
items.note: No base case leads to infinite recursion and StackOverflowError
items.body: A recursive method has a base case (stops) and a recursive call on a smaller problem

items.name: Recursion template
items.body: `type f(n) { if (n == base) return value; return combine(n, f(n - 1)); }`

items.name: Recursion and the call stack
items.body: Each call creates a stack frame holding its parameters and locals; frames are removed on return

items.name: Recursion versus iteration
items.body:
Recursion: simpler code, extra stack space O(depth);
iteration: loop, usually O(1) space

items.name: Factorial (recursive)
items.note: n + 1 calls for factorial(n)
items.body: `long f(int n) { return n == 0 ? 1 : n * f(n - 1); }`

items.name: Fibonacci (recursive)
items.note: The number of calls grows exponentially: O(2^n)
items.body: `int f(int n) { return n <= 1 ? n : f(n - 1) + f(n - 2); }`

items.name: GCD (recursive)
items.note: Euclid's algorithm
items.body: `int gcd(int a, int b) { return b == 0 ? a : gcd(b, a % b); }`

items.name: Power (recursive)
items.note: n + 1 calls. For negative n, use 1 / pow(x, -n)
items.body: `double pow(double x, int n) { return n == 0 ? 1 : x * pow(x, n - 1); }`

items.name: Fast power (recursive)
items.note: O(log n) multiplications. n / 2 is integer division, which suits both even and odd n
items.body:
`double pow(double x, int n) {`
`    if (n == 0) return 1;`
`    double h = pow(x, n / 2);`
`    return n % 2 == 0 ? h * h : x * h * h;`
`}`

items.name: Sum of digits (recursive)
items.body: `int sd(int n) { return n == 0 ? 0 : n % 10 + sd(n / 10); }`

items.name: Reverse a number (recursive)
items.note: Call as rev(n, 0)
items.body: `int rev(int n, int r) { return n == 0 ? r : rev(n / 10, r * 10 + n % 10); }`

items.name: Sum of first n numbers (recursive)
items.body: `int s(int n) { return n == 0 ? 0 : n + s(n - 1); }`

items.name: Binomial coefficient (recursive)
items.body: `int c(int n, int r) { return r == 0 || r == n ? 1 : c(n - 1, r - 1) + c(n - 1, r); }`

items.name: Prime test (recursive)
items.note: Call as isPrime(n, 2) for n >= 2
items.body:
`boolean isPrime(int n, int i) {`
`    if (i * i > n) return true;`
`    if (n % i == 0) return false;`
`    return isPrime(n, i + 1);`
`}`

items.name: Decimal to base b (recursive)
items.note: Appends remainders after the recursive call, so they come out in correct order
items.body: `String conv(int n, int b) { return n == 0 ? "" : conv(n / b, b) + digit(n % b); }`

items.name: Binary search (recursive)
items.note: Array sorted ascending. mid is an int, so the division drops the half, as it should
items.body:
`int bs(int[] a, int k, int lo, int hi) {`
`    if (lo > hi) return -1;`
`    int mid = (lo + hi) / 2;`
`    if (a[mid] == k) return mid;`
`    return k < a[mid] ? bs(a, k, lo, mid - 1) : bs(a, k, mid + 1, hi);`
`}`

items.name: String reverse (recursive)
items.body: `String rev(String s) { return s.length() <= 1 ? s : rev(s.substring(1)) + s.charAt(0); }`

items.name: Palindrome string (recursive)
items.body:
`boolean pal(String s) {`
`    if (s.length() <= 1) return true;`
`    if (s.charAt(0) != s.charAt(s.length() - 1)) return false;`
`    return pal(s.substring(1, s.length() - 1));`
`}`

items.name: Sum of an array (recursive)
items.body: `int sum(int[] a, int n) { return n == 0 ? 0 : a[n - 1] + sum(a, n - 1); }`

items.name: Tower of Hanoi algorithm
items.note: Never place a larger disk on a smaller one
items.body: hanoi(n, from, to, aux): if `n=1` move disk 1 from→ to else: hanoi(n-1,from,aux,to); move disk n; hanoi(n-1,aux,to,from)

items.name: Tower of Hanoi moves
items.note: 3 disks: 7 moves; 4 disks: 15; time O(2^n)
items.body:
`long moves(int n) { return n == 0 ? 0 : 2 * moves(n - 1) + 1; }`
This comes to `(1L << n) - 1`

items.name: Inheritance syntax
items.note: Sub (derived/child) reuses members of Super (base/parent)

`super(args)`: call superclass constructor (first statement);

items.note: index() raises ValueError if x is absent

items.name: remove()
items.note: Removes the first occurrence of x; ValueError if absent

items.name: pop()
items.note: IndexError on an empty list
items.body: `L.pop()` removes and returns the last item; `L.pop(i)` the item at i

items.name: reverse()
items.note: Reverses in place and returns None

items.name: sort() and sorted()
items.note: Use reverse=True for descending order

items.name: min(), max(), sum()
items.note: Mean of numeric list: sum(L) / len(L)

items.name: Linear search in a list
items.note: Worst case n comparisons
items.body: `for i in range(len(L)): if L[i] == key: found at i`

items.name: Frequency of an element
items.note: Or loop and increment a counter

items.name: Tuples are immutable
items.note: Items cannot be assigned, added or removed

items.name: Tuple operations
items.note: Indexing, slicing, concatenation, repetition, membership as for lists

items.name: Tuple built-in functions
items.note: sorted(t) returns a list, not a tuple

items.name: Tuple assignment (unpacking)
items.note: Number of names must equal the number of items
items.body: `a, b = b, a`, `x, y, z = t`

items.name: Mutable item inside a tuple
items.body: A tuple holding a list cannot change which list it refers to, but the list itself can change

items.name: List versus tuple
items.body: List: `[ ]`, mutable; tuple: `( )`, immutable, faster, usable as dictionary key

items.name: Mean, min and max of a sequence
items.note: Works for lists and tuples. In Python / always gives a float, unlike Java

items.name: Binary tree
items.note: Root has no parent; empty tree has no nodes
items.body: Binary tree: every node has at most 2 children (left child and right child)

items.name: Tree terminology
items.body:
Root, parent, child, siblings (same parent), leaf/external node
(no child), internal node (at least one child)

items.name: Degree of a node and of a tree
items.note: In a binary tree every node has degree 0, 1 or 2
items.body:
Degree of a node: its number of children
Degree of a tree: the largest node degree

items.name: Level of a node
items.note: Some textbooks start at level 1; follow your textbook consistently

items.name: Depth of a node
items.note: The depth of a tree is the depth of its deepest node
items.body: `depth(v)`: the number of edges from the root to v, the same as `level(v)`

items.name: Height of a node and of a tree
items.note: A leaf has height 0; single-node tree has height 0
items.body:
`height(v)`: edges on the longest path from v down to a leaf
Height of a tree: `height(root)`

items.name: Height recursion
items.body: `int h(Node v) { return v == null ? -1 : 1 + Math.max(h(v.left), h(v.right)); }`

items.name: Size of a tree
items.body: `int size(Node t) { return t == null ? 0 : 1 + size(t.left) + size(t.right); }`

items.name: Subtree
items.body: Subtree of `v=v` together with all its descendants

items.name: Edges in a tree
items.note: n = number of nodes

items.name: Maximum nodes at a level
items.note: Root is level 0
items.body: `1 << l`, which is 2 to the power l

items.name: Maximum nodes in a tree of given height
items.note: h = height in edges; if height counts levels (root = 1), it is (1 << h) - 1

items.name: Minimum height of a binary tree
items.note: n nodes; maximum height is n - 1 (skewed tree)

items.name: Leaves and degree-2 nodes
items.note: n0 = leaves, n2 = nodes with two children

items.name: Full (strict) binary tree
items.body: Every node has 0 or 2 children: `n == 2 * n0 - 1`, with `n0 - 1` internal nodes

items.name: Perfect binary tree
items.body: All levels full: `(1 << (h + 1)) - 1` nodes and `1 << h` leaves

items.name: Complete binary tree height
items.note: Levels filled left to right. The cast rounds down

items.name: Skewed binary tree
items.body: Every node has one child only: height is `n - 1`

items.name: Traversal cost
items.body: Each traversal visits every node once: O(n)

items.name: Rebuilding a tree from traversals
items.note: Inorder with preorder or postorder gives a unique tree
items.body: Preorder (first) or postorder (last) gives the root; inorder splits left and right subtrees

items.name: Linearithmic
items.note: e.g. efficient sorts

items.name: Quadratic
items.note: e.g. bubble sort

items.name: Input size and basic operations
items.latex: T(n)=\text{number of basic operations as a function of input size }n
items.note: Complexity ignores machine speed

items.name: Big-O definition
items.latex: f(n)=O(g(n))\iff\exists\,c>0,\ n_0:\ f(n)\le c\,g(n)\ \ \forall n\ge n_0

items.name: Dominant term rule
items.latex: \text{Keep the fastest-growing term and drop constants: }3n^{2}+5n+2=O(n^{2})

items.name: Cubic time
items.note: e.g. multiplication of two n x n matrices (three nested loops)

items.name: Exponential time
items.note: e.g. recursive Fibonacci, Tower of Hanoi

items.name: Factorial time
items.note: e.g. generating all permutations

items.name: Triangular nested loop
items.note: Inner loop runs i times for each i
items.body:
Inner loop runs i times for each i: `n * (n + 1) / 2` in all
$O(n^{2})$

items.name: Loop with doubling inside a linear loop
items.latex: \text{Outer }n\text{ times, inner doubling to }n:\ O(n\log n)

items.name: Best, average and worst case
items.latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{Best case: minimum work;\ worst case: maximum work;\ average }\\&\text{case: typical input}\end{aligned}
items.note: Big-O normally quotes the worst case

items.name: Selection sort cases
items.note: Always n(n-1)/2 comparisons

items.name: Access, insert and delete in an array
Matrix operation complexity
items.note: For n x n matrices

items.name: Solving linear equations complexity
items.note: Back substitution alone is O(n^2)

items.name: Factorial and series sums complexity
items.body:
A loop computing a factorial, or the sum of 1 to n: $O(n)$
Closed form `n * (n + 1) / 2`: $O(1)$

items.name: Power computation complexity
items.body:
`Math.pow(x, n)` by repeated multiplication: $O(n)$
Fast power: $O(\log n)$

items.name: Recurrence: T(n) = T(n/2) + 1
items.note: e.g. binary search

items.name: Recurrence: T(n) = 2T(n-1) + 1
items.note: e.g. Tower of Hanoi

items.name: String concatenation in a loop
items.note: Each String concatenation copies the whole string
